def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:

    y = QuantumRegister(1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:
    x, y = QuantumRegister(n), QuantumRegister(1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

    # |0> --H--> |+> --Z--> |->
    qc.h(y[0])
    qc.z(y[0])

    # phase kickback
    qc.compose(o, inplace=True)

    # undo |- > preparation: Z then H brings |- > back to |0>
    qc.z(y[0])
    qc.h(y[0])

    return qc

def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:
    x = QuantumRegister(n)

    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

    # |0> --H--> |+> --Z--> |->

    # apply the given oracle with an explicit qubit mapping

    qargs = [x[i] for i in range(n)] + [y[0]]
    qc.append(o, qargs=qargs)

    # unprepare |- > : Z then H brings it back to |0>
    qc.z(y[0])
    qc.h(y[0])

    return qc

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, QuantumRegister

def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:
    x = QuantumRegister(n)
    y = QuantumRegister(1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

    # |0> --H--> |+> --Z--> |->
    qc.h(y[0])
    qc.z(y[0])

    # oracle with reversed x ordering to match the little-endian convention
    # qargs = [x[n-1],...,x[0], y[0]]  ->  first n wires of o are the x wires
    qargs = [x[n - 1 - i] for i in range(n)] + [y[0]]
    qc.append(o, qargs=qargs)

    # unprepare |->
    qc.z(y[0])
    qc.h(y[0])

    return qc
